title: U.S. House · Arkansas's 1st District
area: Eastern Arkansas (the Arkansas Delta), including Jonesboro, West Memphis, and Forrest City.

context.text: Both party primaries for this seat were canceled after only one candidate filed in each: incumbent Rick Crawford (R) and Terri Yarbrough Green (D) each advanced unopposed. Steve Parsons advanced as the Libertarian Party nominee from a February 22, 2026 party convention.

candidates.name: Rick Crawford

summary.text: Rick Crawford is the Republican nominee and incumbent U.S. Representative for Arkansas's 1st District, seeking re-election.

background.text: Served in the U.S. Army from 1985 to 1989, reaching the rank of sergeant.
Earned a B.S. in agriculture business and economics from Arkansas State University in 1996.
Worked as a news anchor, agriculture reporter, and marketing manager before his election to Congress.

priorities.text: As a member of the House Committee on Agriculture, says supporting the farm safety net for producers facing crop failure, climate fluctuation, natural disaster, and market downturns is his primary focus in writing the next Farm Bill.

Says insurance companies should be able to sell plans across state lines and supports expanding Health Savings Accounts and Flexible Spending Accounts to give people more control over health care decisions.

positions.summary: Says the Affordable Care Act took control away from patients, raised premiums and deductibles, and should be repealed and replaced with patient-centered health care.
positions.quote: The Affordable Care Act takes control away from patients, has led to higher health care costs, and restricts accessibility to care.

positions.summary: Cosponsored H.R. 7296, the SAVE America Act, which requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections and photo identification to vote.
Cosponsored H.R. 722, the Life at Conception Act, which declares that the constitutional right to life is vested in each human being at all stages of life, including the moment of fertilization.

record.text: Has served on House committees during his tenure, including committee assignments renewed each Congress since first taking office in 2011.
Introduced the Cuba Agricultural Exports Act, which would repeal restrictions on financing and marketing that limit U.S. agricultural exports to Cuba.

candidates.researchNotes: No distinct 2026 campaign issues page was found; positions and priorities are drawn from the issue pages and press releases on Crawford's official House site, some of which have not been updated with dated statements in recent years.

summary.text: Terri Yarbrough Green is the Democratic nominee for Arkansas's 1st Congressional District. She is a semi-retired MD pathologist running on campaign finance reform and universal healthcare.

background.text: Graduated from Burges High School and earned a bachelor's degree from Baylor University in 1977.
Describes herself as the daughter of a high school football coach/athletic director.

priorities.text: Says she is "not a politician" but an ordinary person who will "stand up for the ordinary people" and restore transparency and accountability to Congress.
priorities.quote: I am not a politician, but am an ordinary person, just like you, who believes in service to their country and will stand up for the ordinary people, unafraid of the power brokers.

priorities.text: Lists campaign finance reform and universal healthcare as the public-policy areas she is personally passionate about.

positions.summary: Listed universal healthcare among the public-policy areas she is personally passionate about in a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey (Dec. 2025).
In a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey submission (Dec. 22, 2025), listed raising the minimum wage and tying it to inflation among her policy priorities.
positions.quote: Raising the minimum wage and tying it to inflation.

candidates.name: Steve Parsons
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Libertarian Party's February 22, 2026 state convention.

summary.text: Steve Parsons (Steven Gene Parsons) is the Libertarian Party nominee for Arkansas's 1st Congressional District, running on cutting inflation through deregulation and tariff elimination, immigration reform, and reducing incarceration.

priorities.text: Cut inflation by eliminating trade tariffs, cutting federal regulations, reducing bureaucracy in visa/green-card processing, and cutting federal spending.
Reform immigration by cutting green-card and work-visa bureaucracy, eliminating tariffs on Latin American goods, and creating a clearer path to legal permanent residency.
Reduce incarceration by shifting resources from prisons to substance-abuse and mental-health treatment.

positions.summary: Campaign website calls for eliminating trade tariffs, citing the cost of the 2018 U.S.-China trade war.
positions.quote: Eliminate trade tariffs (the 2018 trade war with China alone costs America $50 billion a year and 166,000 jobs).
